extraction.name: PIQA
extraction.description: Physical Interaction: Question Answering (PIQA) is a benchmark dataset for evaluating language representations on their knowledge of physical commonsense. The task is multiple choice question answering: given a question and two possible solutions, a model or a human must choose the most appropriate solution.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi
extraction.publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence
extraction.citeAs: Bisk, Y., Zellers, R., Le Bras, R., Gao, J., & Choi, Y. (2020). PIQA: Reasoning about Physical Commonsense in Natural Language.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Annotators were prompted with links to instructables.com. They were asked to glance at the instructions of an instructable and pull out or have it inspire them to construct two component tasks. They would then articulate the goal (often centered on atypical materials) and how to achieve it. In addition, they were asked to provide a permutation to their own solution which makes it invalid (a trick).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The AFLite algorithm was used to remove stylistic artifacts and trivial examples from the data. It discards instances whose given feature representations are collectively highly indicative of the target label.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed from the data. The AFLite algorithm was used to remove annotation artifacts and bias.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were prompted with instructables and asked to provide a physical goal, a valid solution, and a trick (a permutation of the solution that makes it invalid). Annotators had to successfully identify well-formed pairs in a qualification HIT (>80%) to participate. Data was collected in batches and validated by other annotators for correctness.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed. This often meant removing correct examples that required expert level knowledge. Annotators used simple linguistic tricks (e.g., negation, numerical changes) or swapped a key action/item. A diff button was included in the interface to highlight differences between solutions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset was cleaned of basic artifacts using the AFLite algorithm to perform systematic data bias reduction. Reporting bias was a concern in the initial data collection, where people were drawn to prototypical solutions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Large pretrained models struggle (77% accuracy) compared to humans (95%). Examples requiring expert level knowledge were removed. Reporting bias can swamp the dataset if unconstrained prompts are used.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking progress in physical commonsense understanding, Training, Testing, Validation
